mp_status: Escalation AI template (not a player chassis)

transformation.rule: robot clip Transform_To*_ROBO on robot.glb, vehicle clip Transform_To*_VEH on vehicle.glb; separate skeletons, the game swaps meshes during the overlap (EVIDENCE_PASS2 section 3)

energon_default.note: robot mesh material EnergonColor default (RE b0d9b22): used for uncustomised characters on robot + vehicle meshes, vehicle FX, boost and faction notifies; never team-tinted

team_colour.behaviour: EnergonColor is NOT team-tinted (RE b0d9b22 TARGETED_PASS5_2026-10-06_energon, CONFIRMED script path): TnCharacterApplier.ExtractColors uses CD.EnergonColor when set, else the robot mesh material default (first slot / MIC chain defining EnergonColor) -> manifests/mp_content/energon_defaults.json; ApplyColorsToMesh writes it to robot + vehicle meshes. Cust_Color_A / Cust_COLOR_B: CD colours when not (0,0,0,255), else the mesh material values (RE (a)).
team_colour.team_energon_colors_usage: class defaults read ONLY by kamikaze-mine fallbacks (TnProjectileKamikazeMine / TnParticleSystemParameterEnergonColor), never for bodies or vehicle FX (RE b0d9b22); body energon = top-level energon_default

notify_semantics.TnAnimNotify_ToggleHidden: robot / vehicle mesh swap points: params.Option when authored (e.g. Toggle_Hide), otherwise the class default; which mesh it targets is script / native (UNKNOWN)
notify_semantics.HmAnimNotify_PlayEffect: params.ParticleSystemTemplate at params.SocketName (Parameters = colour / size params)
